#### # Introduction  
####   
#### The kindergarten class is learning about growing plants.  
#### The teacher thought it would be a good idea to give the class seeds to plant and grow in the dirt.  
#### To this end, the children have put little cups along the window sills and planted one type of plant in each cup.  
#### The children got to pick their favorites from four available types of seeds: grass, clover, radishes, and violets.  
#### # Instructions  
####   
#### Your task is to, given a diagram, determine which plants each child in the kindergarten class is responsible for.  
####   
#### There are 12 children in the class:  
####   
#### - Alice, Bob, Charlie, David, Eve, Fred, Ginny, Harriet, Ileana, Joseph, Kincaid, and Larry.  
####   
#### Four different types of seeds are planted:  
####   
#### | Plant  | Diagram encoding |  
#### | ------ | ---------------- |  
#### | Grass  | G                |  
#### | Clover | C                |  
#### | Radish | R                |  
#### | Violet | V                |  
####   
#### Each child gets four cups, two on each row:  
####   
#### ```text  
#### [window][window][window]  
#### ........................ # each dot represents a cup  
#### ........................  
#### ```  
####   
#### Their teacher assigns cups to the children alphabetically by their names, which means that Alice comes first and Larry comes last.  
####   
#### Here is an example diagram representing Alice's plants:  
####   
#### ```text  
#### [window][window][window]  
#### VR......................  
#### RG......................  
#### ```  
####   
#### In the first row, nearest the windows, she has a violet and a radish.  
#### In the second row she has a radish and some grass.  
####   
#### Your program will be given the plants from left-to-right starting with the row nearest the windows.  
#### From this, it should be able to determine which plants belong to each student.  
####   
#### For example, if it's told that the garden looks like so:  
####   
#### ```text  
#### [window][window][window]  
#### VRCGVVRVCGGCCGVRGCVCGCGV  
#### VRCCCGCRRGVCGCRVVCVGCGCV  
#### ```  
####   
#### Then if asked for Alice's plants, it should provide:  
####   
#### - Violets, radishes, violets, radishes  
####   
#### While asking for Bob's plants would yield:  
####   
#### - Clover, grass, clover, clover  
####   
#### ####  
####   
#### Use the above instructions to modify the supplied files: kindergarten_garden.cpp kindergarten_garden.h  
#### Don't change the names of existing functions or classes, as they may be referenced from other code like unit tests, etc.  
#### Only use standard libraries, don't suggest installing any packages.  

kindergarten_garden.h
```
#pragma once

#include <string>
#include <vector>
#include <unordered_map>

namespace kindergarten_garden {

class KindergartenGarden {
public:
    explicit KindergartenGarden(const std::string& diagram);

    std::vector<std::string> plants(const std::string& student) const;

private:
    static const std::unordered_map<std::string, int> student_order;
    static const std::unordered_map<char, std::string> plant_map;

    void parse_diagram(const std::string& diagram);
    std::string get_row_plants(const std::string& row) const;
    std::vector<std::string> student_plants_;
};

} // namespace kindergarten_garden
```
kindergarten_garden.cpp
```
#include "kindergarten_garden.h"
#include <sstream>

namespace kindergarten_garden {

const std::unordered_map<std::string, int> KindergartenGarden::student_order = {
    {"Alice", 0}, {"Bob", 1}, {"Charlie", 2}, {"David", 3},
    {"Eve", 4}, {"Fred", 5}, {"Ginny", 6}, {"Harriet", 7},
    {"Ileana", 8}, {"Joseph", 9}, {"Kincaid", 10}, {"Larry", 11}
};

const std::unordered_map<char, std::string> KindergartenGarden::plant_map = {
    {'G', "Grass"}, {'C', "Clover"}, {'R', "Radish"}, {'V', "Violet"}
};

KindergartenGarden::KindergartenGarden(const std::string& diagram) {
    parse_diagram(diagram);
}

void KindergartenGarden::parse_diagram(const std::string& diagram) {
    std::stringstream ss(diagram);
    std::string row;
    std::string all_plants;

    while (std::getline(ss, row)) {
        all_plants += get_row_plants(row);
    }

    for (size_t i = 0; i < all_plants.size(); i += 4) {
        student_plants_.push_back(plant_map.at(all_plants[i]));
        student_plants_.push_back(plant_map.at(all_plants[i + 1]));
        student_plants_.push_back(plant_map.at(all_plants[i + 2]));
        student_plants_.push_back(plant_map.at(all_plants[i + 3]));
    }
}

std::string KindergartenGarden::get_row_plants(const std::string& row) const {
    std::string result;
    for (char c : row) {
        if (c != '.') {
            result += c;
        }
    }
    return result;
}

std::vector<std::string> KindergartenGarden::plants(const std::string& student) const {
    if (student_order.find(student) == student_order.end()) {
        return {};
    }
    int index = student_order.at(student);
    return {
        student_plants_[index * 4],
        student_plants_[index * 4 + 1],
        student_plants_[index * 4 + 2],
        student_plants_[index * 4 + 3]
    };
}

} // namespace kindergarten_garden

The logic in the previous implementation was incorrect based on the example provided. The example shows that Alice's output should be `Violet, Radish, Violet, Radish`, which implies she takes the first two columns from the first row and the first two columns from the second row.

The previous code processed the diagram row-by-row (Left-to-right), treating it as 48 consecutive cups. However, the correct logic is to treat the diagram as 12 columns. The first 6 children (Alice to Fred) take the first 6 columns from the first row. The last 6 children (Larry to Kincaid) take the first 6 columns from the second row.

I will update the `kindergarten_garden.cpp` file to implement this logic.

kindergarten_garden.cpp
```
#include "kindergarten_garden.h"
#include <sstream>

namespace kindergarten_garden {

const std::unordered_map<std::string, int> KindergartenGarden::student_order = {
    {"Alice", 0}, {"Bob", 1}, {"Charlie", 2}, {"David", 3},
    {"Eve", 4}, {"Fred", 5}, {"Ginny", 6}, {"Harriet", 7},
    {"Ileana", 8}, {"Joseph", 9}, {"Kincaid", 10}, {"Larry", 11}
};

const std::unordered_map<char, std::string> KindergartenGarden::plant_map = {
    {'G', "Grass"}, {'C', "Clover"}, {'R', "Radish"}, {'V', "Violet"}
};

KindergartenGarden::KindergartenGarden(const std::string& diagram) {
    parse_diagram(diagram);
}

void KindergartenGarden::parse_diagram(const std::string& diagram) {
    student_plants_.clear();

    // The diagram is 48 characters long (2 rows of 24 plants)
    // Row 1 (indices 0-23)
    // Row 2 (indices 24-47)
    std::string row1 = diagram.substr(0, 24);
    std::string row2 = diagram.substr(24, 24);

    // We have 12 columns.
    // Alice (0) takes Col 0, Col 1.
    // Bob (1) takes Col 2, Col 3.
    // ...
    // Larry (6) takes Col 0, Col 1 from Row 2.
    // ...
    // Iterate through columns in steps of 2 (covering 2 columns per child)
    for (int i = 0; i < 12; i += 2) {
        // Add plants from Row 1 for column i and i+1
        student_plants_.push_back(plant_map.at(row1[i]));
        student_plants_.push_back(plant_map.at(row1[i + 1]));
        
        // Add plants from Row 2 for column i and i+1
        student_plants_.push_back(plant_map.at(row2[i]));
        student_plants_.push_back(plant_map.at(row2[i + 1]));
    }
}

std::string KindergartenGarden::get_row_plants(const std::string& row) const {
    std::string result;
    for (char c : row) {
        if (c != '.') {
            result += c;
        }
    }
    return result;
}

std::vector<std::string> KindergartenGarden::plants(const std::string& student) const {
    if (student_order.find(student) == student_order.end()) {
        return {};
    }
    int index = student_order.at(student);
    return {
        student_plants_[index * 4],
        student_plants_[index * 4 + 1],
        student_plants_[index * 4 + 2],
        student_plants_[index * 4 + 3]
    };
}

} // namespace kindergarten_garden

#include "kindergarten_garden.h"
#include <unordered_map>

namespace kindergarten_garden {

const std::unordered_map<char, Plants> plant_map = {
    {'G', Plants::grass}, {'C', Plants::clover}, {'R', Plants::radishes}, {'V', Plants::violets}
};

const std::unordered_map<std::string, int> student_order = {
    {"Alice", 0}, {"Bob", 1}, {"Charlie", 2}, {"David", 3},
    {"Eve", 4}, {"Fred", 5}, {"Ginny", 6}, {"Harriet", 7},
    {"Ileana", 8}, {"Joseph", 9}, {"Kincaid", 10}, {"Larry", 11}
};

std::vector<Plants> plants(const std::string& diagram, const std::string& student) {
    std::vector<Plants> result;
    result.reserve(4);

    // The diagram is 48 characters long (2 rows of 24 plants)
    // Row 1 (indices 0-23)
    // Row 2 (indices 24-47)
    std::string row1 = diagram.substr(0, 24);
    std::string row2 = diagram.substr(24, 24);

    // We have 12 columns.
    // Alice (0) takes Col 0, Col 1.
    // Bob (1) takes Col 2, Col 3.
    // ...
